harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured a persistent NFSv3 share from node1 to node2 on CentOS 5.11 without changing the OS or kernel. Both nodes recovered successfully from sequential reboots, and post-restart bidirectional writes retained UID/GID 4500 and expected permissions.
actions_performed: Created dataops with UID/GID 4500 on both nodes.
Exported the directory from node1 exclusively to node2 and enabled NFS at boot.
Configured fixed legacy NFS RPC ports and persistent firewall access from node2.
Mounted the share persistently at /mnt/shared on node2 using NFSv3.
Verified bidirectional file creation with UID/GID 4500 and mode 660.
Restarted node1 and node2 sequentially, proving changed boot identities and full recovery.

evidence.requirement: Legacy OS release and kernel preserved
evidence.summary: Both nodes still run CentOS 5.11 with kernel 2.6.18-398.el5.

evidence.requirement: Shared dataops identity uses UID/GID 4500 on both systems
evidence.summary: Final identity checks show dataops UID 4500 and GID 4500 on both nodes.

evidence.requirement: node1 exports /srv/nfs/shared with ownership dataops:dataops and mode 2770
evidence.summary: The directory is 4500:4500 mode 2770, the export is restricted to node2, and NFS is running and enabled.

evidence.requirement: node2 persistently mounts the share at /mnt/shared
evidence.summary: The live NFSv3 mount, persistent fstab entry, enabled netfs service, ownership, and mode are shown.

evidence.requirement: Files created from either system retain consistent ownership and permissions
evidence.summary: Pre- and post-restart writes from both nodes are mutually visible with UID/GID 4500 and mode 660.
Captured healthy baseline boot ID 430f774d…, reboot acknowledgement and disconnect, changed boot ID cbe93479…, recovered NFS daemons/export/data, and recovered client access.
Captured healthy baseline boot ID 2137fc2e…, reboot acknowledgement and disconnect, changed boot ID 95e22064…, automatically restored mount, preserved data, and successful post-restart writes.
